criteria.requirement: The tool must support role-based access for the originator (Sailor/LPO), Division Officer, Department Head, Engineer Officer/CHENG, XO, and CO as releasing authority, with each role able to comment, return for revision, or approve and forward. Drafts must enforce NWP 1-03.1 CASREP formatting (report types such as INITIAL, UPDATE, CORRECT, and CASCOR, plus category and required fields), keep a full version history and audit trail of every comment and approval, and show at a glance where each report is in the routing chain. The prototype must use notional, unclassified data only.
criteria.detail: The complete synthetic CASREP uses all six simulated roles, required fields, categories 2/3/4 and INITIAL/UPDATE/CORRECT/CASCOR previews; a returned draft is revised, reviewed and simulated-released with visible holder, comments and revision-bound approvals. Linked amendments preserve released snapshots. This demonstrates assumed format checks only, not validated NWP 1-03.1 compliance or operational rules. — demonstrated by route-return-release, invalid-fields, stale-approval, local-draft, linked-lifecycle at both viewport sizes.

criteria.requirement: Reject invalid state transitions and stale approvals.
criteria.detail: Out-of-order CO release and dirty-form review are rejected; content changes invalidate earlier approvals and require a new complete route before simulated release. — demonstrated by stale-approval, local-draft at both viewport sizes.

Two competing amendments visibly retain restoration 20:00Z and the fictional seal-kit request; unresolved conflict blocks release, explicit reconciliation retains both parents through reload and exports their history with the final release. — demonstrated by conflict-recovery at both viewport sizes.

An evaluator can perform intake, comment, return, revise, all approvals and local export, and recover invalid inputs without losing the draft. Automated journeys do not claim that a human reviewer has accepted the workflow. — demonstrated by route-return-release, release-package, invalid-fields at both viewport sizes.

criteria.requirement: A working prototype that walks one mock CASREP from initial draft through every approval role to CO release, including at least one "returned for revision" loop. Teams should also submit a short demo video or live walkthrough and a one-page brief covering the role/permission model, how the tool would handle classification and integration with existing Navy messaging systems, and what it would take to field it.
criteria.detail: One mock CASREP traverses Sailor/LPO, Division Officer, Department Head, Engineer Officer/CHENG, XO and CO with a return loop. Named synthetic message/history downloads, a live walkthrough and a one-page fielding brief cover permissions, classification, Navy messaging boundaries and fielding prerequisites; release remains a local simulation. — demonstrated by route-return-release, conflict-recovery, release-package at both viewport sizes.
